bluf: The packets describe political allegations, official scrutiny, a fatal train crash and other developments, but most do not specify when the events occurred. Each item has one source; E7 provides no substantive details, and the reported allegations and claims are not independently corroborated in these packets.

items.text: The Guardian reported that 69 people were confirmed dead in a train crash in Spain, with at least 70 reported missing; Sánchez said people of 27 nationalities may be among the dead or injured. The crash date was not stated.
According to France 24, Likud alleged without providing evidence that voter fraud partly drove Arab parties’ record gains in Israel’s election this week; the parties could become kingmakers.

The Guardian reported that members of Congress sent federal immigration officials a letter this week seeking answers about conditions at a Texas detention facility, where hunger-striking immigrants said they faced threats of force-feeding.

The Guardian reported that Sudanese diaspora members and human-rights monitors denounced an Emirati diplomat’s candidacy for a top UN job, citing allegations that the UAE supports Sudan’s paramilitary RSF and her denial of those accusations.

The Guardian reported that Swedish climate academic Andreas Malm criticized a UK travel ban after the government revoked his travel authorization; he said he had been kept in the dark about the decision.

The Guardian reported that Hong Kong’s leader apologized for government shortcomings that contributed to a residential fire last year that killed 168 people; some survivors and bereaved families said justice remained unserved.
Reuters, citing sources, reported that Microsoft expects to raise $25 billion in a US bond sale; the timing was not stated.
